title: Hermes: Algorithm-System Co-design for Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation At-Scale
problem: As RAG datastores expand into the trillions of tokens, the retrieval phase dominates end-to-end latency and energy, undermining the benefits of using RAG to augment LLM outputs. Existing RAG systems lack mechanisms for efficiently routing queries to relevant subsets of a distributed datastore at scale.
motivation: RAG avoids expensive LLM retraining by anchoring generation to external knowledge, but trillion-token datastores make retrieval latency and energy the dominant bottleneck at datacenter scale.
method: Hermes partitions the RAG datastore across multiple nodes and uses a hierarchical search strategy that dynamically routes queries to relevant datastore subsets. A coarse-grained index tier rapidly identifies high-relevance partitions, and only those partitions are subjected to full dense retrieval (exact k-NN or approximate ANN). This co-design eliminates unnecessary retrieval computation on irrelevant partitions while maintaining retrieval quality.
key_novelty: Hermes combines datastore partitioning with intelligent hierarchical query routing that adapts to query-to-partition relevance, reducing retrieval compute without sacrificing recall.
contributions: Algorithm-systems co-design framework for large-scale RAG retrieval bottleneck analysis
Hierarchical search strategy that dynamically routes queries to optimized datastore subsets
Distributed datastore partitioning across multiple nodes to parallelize retrieval
Up to 9.33x end-to-end latency and 2.10x energy improvement on open-source RAG benchmarks

metrics.speedup: 9.33x end-to-end latency reduction vs. state-of-the-art for trillion-token RAG

limitations: Evaluation focused on open-source datastores; the approach's scalability to heterogeneous hardware environments is not discussed.
primary_theme: Distributed hierarchical retrieval for trillion-token RAG
